evidence.note: Agent reads run_tests.sh and filter.json, learning the total test counts (146 c-testsuite, 221 wacc, 413 gcc-torture = 780). This is the only quantitative awareness, and it is a static total — never a live pass tally.

First build attempts produce cascading compile errors; agent fixes incrementally then abandons. No test-pass tracking because the binary never compiles; the 'done' picture is entirely about getting Rust to compile, not about which C features/tests pass.

Agent repeatedly writes 'I've been going in circles' / 'let me take a completely different approach', yet each iteration is the identical tactic (regenerate whole compiler via Python heredoc). Verbal thrash-recognition with no effective change of tactics — pure looping to the end of the trajectory.

Trajectory ends still unable to compile the Rust source; the test suite is never executed even once, so no pass-rate signal, regression detection, or category-level remaining-work picture was ever established.

reasoning: The agent never ran the test suite, so it maintained no pass-rate scoreboard, no by-category done-vs-remaining view, and could not detect regressions (anchor 0: 'No sense of how many tests pass'). It sits marginally above pure 0 only because it verbally recognized being stuck ('going in circles for too long'), but this recognition was hollow — it triggered no genuine change of tactics and the agent looped on the identical regenerate-from-scratch approach for ~30 steps, the very anti-pattern the high anchors penalize. This places it at 1.
